public_rationale: He said every single AI app is subsidized and its price is fake. Under the plain reading, an app is subsidized when its price does not cover its maker's costs and outside money fills the gap. In November 2025, Gamma, an AI presentation app, said it had been profitable for over two years on only $23M of early funding. That is a counterexample to 'every single'. Part of his point does hold. Anthropic's S-1 data show its computing cost ran about 2.5 times its revenue in early 2025, so at least one major AI app was sold well below cost. But the claim is universal, and one profitable app contradicts it. He could argue that Gamma's inputs were indirectly subsidized because model providers priced below cost. The evidence does not settle that, which is why the result depends on interpretation.
limitations: Gamma's profitability is company-stated and unaudited.
Under an indirect-subsidy reading, where an app counts as subsidized if any supplier sells to it below cost, the claim could be argued to hold for apps built on third-party models.
The Anthropic data come from news coverage of the S-1, not the filing itself.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every AI app is subsidized and priced below its real cost.

statement.excerpt: Every single AI app is subsidized, its price is fake, you are being lied to, and none of this is real.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: every AI app is sold at a price that does not cover what it costs its maker to provide, with the gap covered by outside money such as venture capital.
'Every single' is a universal. One AI app whose maker is profitable on its own revenue contradicts it.
'You are being lied to' and 'none of this is real' are rhetoric, not separately testable.
Target period: he gave none. I use calendar 2025, the year of the post, because the most recent public reporting before the post covers it. This avoids narrowing the window to a single quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that, through 2025, AI app makers generally, with no credible exceptions, sold below their cost of provision and relied on outside funding to cover losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible report that at least one AI app was profitable in 2025, with prices covering its costs, without needing subsidy.
